Question:  Do the JWs have their own bible?  Yes, it is called the "New World Translation" (NWT).
  It is fair to say that this translation is not well respected by Scripture scholars outside of the
 JW organization.  Some say that the NWT appears to be mostly a modification of English
 versions of the Bible that had already existed, and that its changes were made so that the JW
 bible would confirm the Witnesses' teachings.

Answer:  A committee of five JW members wrote the first edition of the NWT.  For some years,
 the names of the members of this committee were kept secret.  But ultimately, two former Witnesses
 (Bill Cetnar and Raymond Franz) leaked the names of the members of this NWT committee.
  It then became known that four of these five members had received NO formal training in
 biblical languages (Hebrew, Aramaic, or ancient Greek), and the fifth member (Frederick Franz,
 who was the fourth president of the Watchtower Society, and who happened to be Raymond
 Franz's uncle) had formally studied non-biblical Greek for only two years.
http://www.stjohncondos.com/catholic/tracts/witnesses.htm
